text: You plug a USB gamepad into your Android phone. The buttons work. But the rumble? Nothing. If that sounds familiar, this video is for you. Meet NeuroPad: a free, open source app that brings rumble back to USB gamepads on Android. And you don't need root.

Here's the problem. When you connect a USB-C gamepad to an Android phone, Android passes the buttons through just fine, but it doesn't pass rumble on to most USB controllers. So the game asks your controller to vibrate, and the motors never get the message.

NeuroPad fixes this with a simple idea. It shows your games a virtual wireless controller, an Xbox or PlayStation pad that Android fully supports. Your real USB gamepad drives that virtual controller. And every rumble the game produces is sent straight back to the motors in your real pad, within a few milliseconds.

And the best part: this is confirmed on real hardware. NeuroPad was tested on a Nothing Phone 2 running Android 16, with a GameSir G8 Plus. Input, the virtual controller, and rumble all work. Users report the Razer Kishi Ultra working too. The problem is fixed.

Let's take a look at the app. The Home screen has one big power button that starts the bridge. A checklist shows system access, your USB gamepad, and the virtual controller at a glance. You choose which controller games should see, and live meters show the heavy and light motors as they rumble. You can even test each motor without opening a game.

There are five controller profiles: Xbox 360, Xbox One, Xbox Series, DualShock 4, and DualSense. Games show the matching button prompts. If one game doesn't rumble with one profile, simply try another.

The Controller tab shows your input live: sticks, triggers and buttons, exactly as they arrive. You can switch to a Nintendo layout or build a fully custom one, including back paddles. And the bridge statistics show how fast it is: about a fifth of a millisecond per packet.

To create a virtual controller, NeuroPad needs the rights of Android's shell user, but not root. On Android 11 or newer, pair once with Wireless debugging and the app sets everything up by itself, no computer required. On any Android version, the one-click PC installer does the job. And rooted phones are supported too. Nothing ever leaves your phone: the app only talks to itself, on 127.0.0.1.

In Settings, you can tune the rumble strength, and stretch very short pulses so small effects are actually felt. Ignore system vibration keeps keyboard taps from shaking your controller. And for games that only vibrate the phone, NeuroPad can mirror that vibration to your gamepad.

Version 2 is a complete open source rewrite, and it fixes the problems people ran into before. Long rumbles are no longer cut off after half a second. Rumble no longer goes missing after a notification. Launcher taps and keyboard clicks no longer shake the gamepad. Short effects are no longer weak, and long rumbles no longer stutter.

NeuroPad works with XInput, or Xbox mode, USB gamepads that have rumble motors. That covers many controllers from GameSir, Razer, 8BitDo, Flydigi, and Microsoft. If your controller has a mode switch, set it to Xbox or XInput.

To get NeuroPad, open the GitHub repository, NeuroPad Virtual GamePad Simulation, and download the latest release. Use the one-click installer if you have a computer nearby, or install the APK straight on the phone on Android 11 and up. Then plug in your gamepad, open NeuroPad, and tap the power button. That's it.

NeuroPad is free, has no ads, and needs no account. If it brought rumble back to your controller, a star on GitHub helps other people find it, and you can support development on Ko-fi or PayPal. Tried it with another controller? Tell us in the comments. Thanks for watching!
